text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Steelmaker Boehler-Uddeholm's chief Claus Raidl is expected to become Creditanstalt's new boss. He is the favoured candidate of Bank Austria, which took over Creditanstalt at the beginning of the year.
- A joint holding of Bank Austria and Creditanstalt is planned to start on January 1, 1998.
- German baking giant Mueller will take over the majority of Austria's leading baker Ankerbrot.
- Economic research institute IHS says wages must be kept low, so that Austria's job market can improve in 1999.
- Conservative Vice-Chancellor Wolfgang Schuessel is strictly against plans to merge Bank Austria and Creditanstalt.

- Austrian oil group OMV's profits went up to a record high of 2.9 billion schillings in 1996. The dividend will be raised from 20 to 23 schillings. The company has shown interest in participation in Austrian provincial energy providers Begas, OKA and Ferngas.
- Brewer BBAG sets its hopes for growth on exports. The company's sale of its Coca-Cola activities brought it profits of 500 million schillings. The dividend for 1996 is to remain constant.
- Austrians have not changed their travel, living and recreational habits due to the government's austerity measures. However expenditure on luxury goods and food is down.
- Austria is losing its top position in trade with eastern Europe. This year there may even be a trade deficit with the region as Austrian exporters lose ground.
- Austria's economic growth was the lowest within the European Union in 1995.
- Austria's anonymous savings accounts have to be abolished within the next two months, otherwise the European Commission has threatened to take legal action against the country.
- Fibremaker Lenzing is planning to take legal action against some of its European competitors, saying they were receiving illegal subsidies.
